title: Listening: types of calendars
competency: Listen to and understand a text about types of calendars.

keywords.def: A system for organising days into weeks, months and years.
A calendar that follows the cycle of the moon; 12 lunar months make about 354 days.
A calendar that follows the sun and the seasons; a year is about 365¼ days.
A calendar whose months follow the moon, with an extra month added sometimes to stay with the seasons.
A calendar whose months follow the moon and whose year is fixed by watching the stars, like the Borana calendar.
A day when people do not work, often shown in red on a calendar.

en.text: A calendar organises days into weeks, months and years. Most calendars follow natural cycles. A lunar calendar follows the moon; a solar calendar follows the sun and seasons; a lunisolar calendar uses moon months but adds a month to stay with the seasons; a lunistellar calendar uses the moon and the stars, like the Borana calendar. Some other calendars follow neither the moon nor the sun.

screens.why: Moon months + an extra month to keep up with the seasons (the sun) = lunisolar.

en.text: The Ethiopian calendar shows important dates. Meskerem 1 is the New Year (Enkutatash), Meskerem 17 is Meskel, Tir 11 is Timket, and Yekatit 23 is the Victory of Adwa. We can group dates into religious holidays, national and historical holidays, and family dates.

screens.text: Why are Fasika and Eid called "moveable" holidays?
opts: Their date changes from year to year because it follows the moon
